set.approach: Take the dead-end Forest Service road 22S19 off Sherman Pass Road to its end, where trail 33E32 begins, and hike south, then turn right (west) on an old logging spur marked by a cairn. Stay on the lower fork, and at a big cairn look left for one on a large stump; that marks the cross-country turn-off, which follows cairns uphill over a subtle ridge. Upper Poison Dome comes into view on the far side, with most routes on its south-southeast side. The route is a sustained bolted line on the south face.

set.approach: Use the roadside pullouts short of Trapper Springs Campground on the reservoir's west shore, then walk uphill west toward the left (south) side of Trapper Dome. At the foot of the South Face, a ramp leads past a fallen dead tree to a shelf that holds the starts of the Upper Tier routes. This one starts right of Good Deed, just right of a black streak.

From the Topanga Lookout trailhead hike down past the old lookout foundation; the top of the slab comes into view, and a little further along use trails drop to its base. The route is down and left from Pebbles; skirt the slab downhill, or work up the lowest slabs to a small level spot beside a big bush, where the bolt line begins.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route, or walk off the top to the Topanga Ridge Trail.

set.approach: From the Topanga Lookout trailhead hike down past the old lookout foundation; the top of the slab comes into view, and a little further along use trails drop to its base. The route follows the newer bolt line on the far right side of the slab.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route, or walk off the top and rejoin the trail.

set.approach: Park in the dirt pullout west of the Tuolumne store along Tioga Road and follow the trail past a creek bed and up the slabs; stay below the summit and work left along the base to Peanut Gallery, a black wall carrying a few bolts. From there a scramble over second- to third-class ground reaches the main climbs. The route follows a black streak just left of Orange Plasma.

Take the signed Castle Rock trail from Highway 18; Yellow Pine Tower is the south-facing formation between the trail and the west side of Castle Rock, downhill from Camelot Crag. It starts either with a dyno off the boulder at the base or by traversing in from the right to a high bolt.
